Crichton came up with the match-winning play in extra time.  (Getty Images: Jason McCawley )

Canterbury have snatched their sixth win of the NRL season to keep their finals hopes alive with skipper Stephen Crichton landing a golden-point field goal for a 13-12 victory over Manly.

Crichton had earlier on Saturday night scored his side's first try at Stadium Australia, but his 82nd-minute effort gave the Bulldogs their third win from the last four games.

That puts some oxygen into their September finals hopes after it was starting to look out of reach after losing five on the trot in April.

The Dogs and Sea Eagles gave their fans plenty of anxiety attacks in the final stages of regulation.

Manly halfback Jamal Fogarty missed two field goal attempts, while Crichton missed his first and then baulked on the second as the defence rushed up in his face.

It had been a wrestle for most of the second half after the away side raced to an 8-0 lead, before Crichton's converted try had Canterbury trailing by two at the break.

Lachlan Galvin's sixth four-pointer of the season got the Bulldogs ahead for the first time in the match on 60 minutes, while Sea Eagles winger Lehi Hopoate's second of the night seven minutes later locked up the scoreboard at 12-12.

Kieran Foran's side had to dig deep after losing prop Kobe Hetherington (concussion) in the 10th minute and then hooker Brandon Wakeham (calf) just after half-time.

If Crichton was trying to push for a return to the NSW Origin team, playing his first game at five-eighth for Canterbury seemed a strange way to do it.

"It's always been an option and he's shown some potential in that position," Bulldogs coach Cameron Ciraldo said Crichton.

"The change was more around helping Burto (Matt Burton) find his best and most consistent form."

Crichton played at five-eighth at NRL level for the first time.  (Getty Images: Jason McCawley )

Manly back-rower Haumole Olakau'atu was up to his usual bullocking best, even though he nursed a left shoulder injury in the second half.

He still pulled off a try-saving tackle on Leo Thompson to underline his credentials for a return to the Blues' side for the July 8 decider at Suncorp Stadium — he was on the extended bench for game two at the MCG.

Sea Eagles fullback Tom Trbojevic gave his left hamstring a good workout in his return after nine weeks on the sidelines, running for 196 metres off 27 runs.

Trbojevic too was on audition for a possible NSW recall. He did little wrong and next week plays Melbourne to further his chances.

Earlier, Gold Coast shocked competition leaders Penrith 19-18 in one of the best and bravest wins in their history as rising half Zane Harrison announced himself as a star.

The 20-year-old's winning field goal at Skilled Park on Saturday night, with 19 seconds left on the clock, was a composed cracker after he set up two second-half tries.

Harrison, playing just his sixth NRL game, was part of a starting side where all 13 players have only played for the Titans.

"He's the real deal that kid," delighted coach Josh Hannay said of Harrison.

"It is a special night for him. That will go in the scrap book for sure, but he is going to have a lot of those moments.

"We see that kid every day train and prepare with composure. It is one thing to do it at training, another to do it in front of 20,000 against the Panthers."

More than 70 old boys of the Titans and former Gold Coast franchises formed a guard of honour as the players ran on the field.

The club celebrated their own retro round with iconic mascot Captain Charger making an appearance for the first time in 19 years.

Zane Harrisonof the Titans celebrates with team mates after kicking a field goal to win the match during the round 16 NRL match between Wests Tigers and Penrith Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium, on June 20, 2026, in Gold Coast, Australia.  (Getty Images: Chris Hyde )

It was fitting that the players should step up and give coach Josh Hannay and their long-suffering fans a win for the ages in their first home match in 49 days.

The Panthers' eight-game winning streak came to an end after they led 12-0 after 14 minutes, but the Titans rallied with defensive grit after losing star lock Cooper Bai early due to a head knock.

ABC Sport Daily is your daily sports conversation. We dive into the biggest story of the day and get you up to speed with everything else that's making headlines.

Penrith, who led 12-6 at halftime, had 32 tackles inside Gold Coast's 20m line before the hosts got down in the opposite danger zone.

"We did start well but we just lost the killer punch or killer instinct," Panthers coach Ivan Cleary said.

The second half started in the same vein but the Titans, to a man, repelled set after set. Five-eighth Jayden Campbell, one of the smallest players on the field, came up with massive defensive hits and plays.

Earlier, the Dolphins beat the Tigers 36-22 despite missing halfback Isaiya Katoa and Maroons players Selwyn Cobbo, Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow, Max Plath and Tom Flegler.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 10:45pm

By Nick Campton

We'll be blogging all three of tomorrow's NRL matches and every game for the rest of the season.

See you next time!

Key Event

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 10:30pm

By Nick Campton

Canterbury coach Cameron Ciraldo is speaking now.

"It wasn't a pretty win, but that's our style of game," Ciraldo said.

He explains what the Bulldogs were looking for by switching Crichton from centre to five-eighth.

"It's always been an option. At times over the past two seasons when we've been short in the halves Critta has jumped in there and he's shown enormous potential in that position," Ciraldo said.

"We've always had that in the back of our minds, that it might happen one day.

"We had the bye last week and had a really good chance to chat about how the first half of the season has gone, how individuals have gone and the change was more around helping Burto find his best and most consistent form."

Says it's aimed at giving Burton less responsibility.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 10:20pm

By Nick Campton

Sea Eagles coach Kieran Foran is speaking now.

"It wasn't too enjoyable, that one. I said to the guys, I was over the moon with the effort and the commitment," Foran said.

"We can hold our heads high in that regard, but I thought we didn't execute at our best. The accumulation of poor error after poor error kept them in the game long enough and eventually that hurts you.

"You keep giving a quality team like Canterbury moment after moment it comes back to bite you.

"We'll get some good takeaway from those moments in the latter stages of the game where we could have managed a set better and given ourselves a better chance to have a genuine shot.

"I don't expect the guys to get it perfect. But I think we should have put the game away before golden point to be honest."

Captain Tom Trbojevic says he pulled up well on return from injury but isn't asked about a potential State of Origin berth for Game III.

Key Event

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:33pm

By Nick Campton

Brown throws a loose pass and Crichton dives on it! What a horror ball! Now the Bulldogs have a chance at the winner.

And this time Crichton makes no mistake! He nails the winner from 35 metres out!

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:31pm

By Nick Campton

The Bulldogs run it on the last, kick inside and Koula just cleans it up but he's trapped in-goal.

The ref goes to the Bunker to make sure there's no interference on the chaser - but Tuala is offside and Manly get a penalty!

Wow, what a turn! The Sea Eagles will have the first chance.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:28pm

By Nick Campton

Manly kick us off. Here we go!

Key Event

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:26pm

By Nick Campton

Manly don't get a shot in! They got too close and in the end they bail out with a bad grubber that goes nowhere!

We're off to golden point.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:24pm

By Nick Campton

Rinakama loses it 30 out from his own line! Canterbury have a challenge and they must use it, the ref said loose carry.

This is massive. I think he's just making the tackle, the challenge doesn't land.

OK, Manly feed, 30 out, one minute left. What've they got?

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:22pm

By Nick Campton

Crichton has another shot but he pulls it right. Manly from the 20 with a seven tackle set. Fogarty can go from distance.....

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:20pm

By Nick Campton

Saab loses the ball under heavy pressure from Burton. I thought he was a disruptor but it's not called and the Bulldogs have a golden chance to take the lead.

Crichton will be the one. He's in the pocket but bails out under pressure, and then he grubbers it to nobody! What was he thinking? Manly ball.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:17pm

By Nick Campton

Tracey goes through of Galvin, he has Tuala in support and as he surges for the line he loses the ball! It was a strip from Tom Trbojevic! Manly ball.

Bit on, my word.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:16pm

By Nick Campton

Manly go wide straight away and Saab is off, he's got Garrick in support and the Bulldogs drag him down but the Sea Eagles are humming.

Fogarty nails a very tricky grubber to force a drop out and on the last tackle he has a field goal, ten out, right in front and he sprays it!

Thought that was automatic! But Canterbury hang on.

Key Event

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:13pm

By Nick Campton

Trbojevic forces a drop out with a nice kick at the end of a power set. Saab gets dragged over the sideline but it's a penalty on Crichton for a second effort.

And, at last, the Dogs crack - Brooks throws a good out-ball to Koula, he sucks in the winger and pops the pass to Hopoate to score his second.

Very classy stuff from Koula, he put a very tasty move on Tuala. Those two have had a good battle all night.

Can Fogarty break the deadlock from out wide? It's only five metres or so in from the sideline.

It takes the post! We're level at 12-all!

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:07pm

By Nick Campton

Ben Trbojevic kicks for himself on the last, three Manly players are bearing down on it and it takes the only bounce where it can miss them all for Tuala to clean it up!

A play later Manly are pinged for offside. The Dogs escape.

Key Event

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:04pm

By Nick Campton

At last, we have more points. A deflected kick on the last, on the attack, gives the Dogs a fresh set after a good run from Galvin from dummy half gets them into the the 20.

In the end the try is really simple, Galvin gets on the outside of Trbojevic and slides over to score. Two nice plays from the halfback.

Crichton converts and it's 12-8 Bulldogs.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 9:01pm

By Nick Campton

A really good defensive set forces the Dogs to kick from their own 30. Can Manly make the most of it?

Nope - Brown loses the ball midway through the set. This game is degenerating.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 8:59pm

By Nick Campton

Koula goes for a tap on that is ruled to go forward and the Dogs have a fresh set on the Manly 40.

But then Jones gives it right back after he loses it in a tackle. Both sides struggling to find their best right now.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 8:56pm

By Nick Campton

Tracey loses the ball and Brooks snaps it up and goes the other way. Manly have a chance at more points.

The attack is stilted, it falls to Olakau'atu on the last, he kicks into the in-goal and corrals Curran behind the line but is called for a high tackle. Close call, but Dogs get an easy passage out.

Sat 20 Jun 2026 at 8:53pm

By Nick Campton

After a sensational set from the Dogs where a Tupouniua inside ball to Tracey gets them right on the attack, Crichton tries to nail a very difficult cut-out pass to an open Rinakama but the winger can't gather it in.
